# Plots
![](images/plotting.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

Many plots of significant associations are created by `maaslin3()` .
The types of plots can be grouped into 3 main types:

1. The summary plot
    - This shows abundance and prevalence modelling information for the top 25 features
2. Linear plots
    - These are for the abundance based linear modelling
    - Box plots are produced for categorical fixed effects
    - Scatter plots with a linear model line are produced for continuous fixed effects
3. Logistics plots
    - These are for the prevalence based logistic modelling
    - Grids are produced for categorical fixed effects
    - Box plots are produced for continuous fixed effects


In your own analysis you would start by looking at the summary plot.
However, we will look at the other plots beforehand to get a better understanding of the coefficient values so we can better interpret the summary plot.

## Notebook setup
![](images/jupiter.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

We'll create one notebook for our plot investigations, meaning it'll be quite large.

Save then close and halt your "3-Text_output.ipynb" notebook.

Create and open a new jupyter notebook called "4-Plots.ipynb".

Create a markdown cell at the top with:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# 4-Plots
## Libraries & data
```

In a code cell load the required libraries and data.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Library
library("maaslin3")
library("IRdisplay")
library("tidyverse")
#Data
load("genus_output/significant_results.RData")
load("metadata.RData")
```
